actions.text: Committee on Veterans' Affairs. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
Committee on Veterans' Affairs. Hearings held. Hearings printed: S.Hrg. 119-247.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

dimensions.assessment: Directly involves federal administrative and oversight personnel within the VA, FEMA, Government Accountability Office, and congressional committees.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall submit to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans' Affairs of the House of Representatives a report

dimensions.assessment: Mandates studies, reviews, and reports to evaluate emergency readiness, inventory management, and interagency coordination without immediately altering operations.
dimensions.evidence: To improve the emergency management capabilities of the Department of Veterans Affairs, and for other purposes.

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative reporting costs with no new appropriations or direct federal spending changes stated.
Requires three distinct reports and plans from the Secretary of Veterans Affairs within 90 to 180 days of enactment.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall submit... a report

dimensions.assessment: Primarily consists of one-time reporting requirements over short timeframes (90 to 180 days post-enactment).
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act

missing_information: Cost of preparing the requested reports and conducting studies
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to submit multiple administrative reports and plans concerning its emergency management offices, regional readiness centers, and coordination/fuel sharing with FEMA.
